notes: arsenal/media/sheet.py sheet() and video_sheet(): many frames or images on one labelled grid (file time, plus game time from a studio.clockmap.v1), long edge <= max_long_edge (1600) so a sheet costs one image read. Video cells are decoded by ffmpeg straight to their final size and pasted unmodified; the index (<png>.json) gives each cell's src, t, pts, crop, size and md5, and frames.at_times(src, [pts], crop, size) returns the same pixels. Every frame is picked by its own pts (packet list) and decoded from the keyframe before it, every seek subtracting the format start_time, so an MPEG-TS (container clock at 1.4 s) gets the same exact frames. video_sheet: 30 keyframes over the 33-min 1080p60 HEVC recording in 3.1-4.1 s, a 120-s span in 1.1-1.2 s (keyframe-only decode); 30 exact times in 9.6 s. A layout that cannot fit max_long_edge, a span outside the file and an unreadable image fail closed with one line. py -m arsenal.media sheet <items...> | --video <v> --n 30.
